subject: Urgent: BrightLoop 5xx/429 spike during peak jobs — capacity lag and retry storm
messages:
From: Michael Tan <michael.t@brightloop.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 18:12:00 -0800
Subject: Latency/5xx spike causing job failures — urgent

Ava —

This morning we saw a sharp spike in 5xx and 429 responses from the Redwood hosted endpoint (text-generation-xl) starting ~17:50 PST. Over a 20 minute window ~12% of requests returned 5xx and there were multiple client-side retries which made the effective traffic look like a surge. A few of our batch jobs failed hard and triggered downstream alerts.

Attaching a small snippet of our client-side logs; we can provide more if helpful. Can you confirm whether this is an autoscaling lag / capacity exhaustion issue on your side? Our SLOs are taking a hit and we need a mitigation plan ASAP — ideally a short-term capacity bump and acknowledgement of a root cause.

Michael
Michael Tan
Head of Platform Engineering, BrightLoop
(michael.t@brightloop.ai)

Subject: Re: Latency/5xx spike causing job failures — urgent

Michael / Ava — preliminary findings from the runtime:

- Around 17:46 PST we observed a sustained increase in queued requests against BrightLoop's Dedicated pool. Token throughput per GPU trended above forecast for a 10-minute window.
- The autoscaler executed but lagged: first scale event at 17:49 and the additional worker nodes reached readiness at ~17:58. There’s a ~9–12 minute cold window where request rate > available slot capacity.
- During that window the serving runtime returned 5xx errors (resource exhaustion) and our admission controller started returning 429s as a protective backpressure signal.
- External retry clients (your side) retried aggressively; we saw retry amplification that pushed sustained utilization higher and hit a transient token-only memory high-water, triggering additional 5xx bursts.

I attached the service aggregation logs and the autoscaler policy dump. Next steps I recommend: temporary immediate capacity bump (hot add + scale policy override), short-term patch to reduce scale-up latency (kernel warm pools), and guidance for client-side retry jitter to avoid synchronized retries.

Attachments: svc-logs-20261127-18-aggregate.gz, scaling-policy-dump.json

Marcus Lin
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Michael Tan <michael.t@brightloop.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 19:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Latency/5xx spike causing job failures — urgent

Team / Michael —

Thanks Marcus, that diagnosis aligns with what I was expecting from our runtime signals. For BrightLoop (customer impact) I propose the following immediate actions:

- Short-term mitigation (next 30–90 minutes):
  * Manually increase BrightLoop Dedicated pool capacity by 2x equivalent vGPU for 2 hours (hot add).
  * Apply a temporary autoscaler override to be more aggressive on ramp-up for scheduled peak windows.
  * Provide BrightLoop recommended client retry jitter and a soft-fail code path to avoid immediate full retries.
- Post-incident remediation (next 7 days):
  * Implement warm kernel pools to reduce cold-start time for new workers.
  * Adjust autoscaler hysteresis and test against synthetic load patterns.
  * Joint postmortem and SLA remediation discussion (credit/terms if needed).

If leadership approves the hot capacity bump I’ll coordinate procurement/ops and authorize the 2-hour reserve. Michael — does BrightLoop want us to proceed with the immediate bump? Also please share whether you want engineering to hold off retries client-side while we apply the bump.

Tessa Morgan
Director, Customer Success
Tessa_Morgan@redwood.ai

Michael —

Quick update and immediate ask:
- We’ve executed a manual hot-add to your Dedicated pool; capacity increased and nodes reported ready at 14:52 PST. Initial metrics show 5xx/429 rates dropping back below your alert threshold.
- We’ve applied a temporary autoscaler override which will remain in effect for the next 2 hours; we’ll monitor and revert once stable.
- Marcus attached runbook and logs; Tessa is coordinating a short joint postmortem next week.

Action items for BrightLoop:
1) If possible, apply client-side exponential backoff with randomized jitter for the next 30 minutes to avoid retry amplification.
2) Confirm whether you want us to proceed with a formal SLA credit and the procurement contact for reconciliation (cc’d procurement@brightloop.ai).

We’re committed to a full postmortem and remediation plan. Apologies for the disruption — we’ll follow up with root cause and timeline for the autoscaler fix.

Thanks,
